questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Wide range of courses taught in English and its near proximity to China.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Some covid restrictions are still in place in Japan. They are not especially strict but make living at a dorm a bit awkward. Other than that undergrad and graduate school are very different, important to note this.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy. One big issue is the language barrier. You will also need to sign a lot of forms many of which are in Japanese.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: A bunch of manuals and e-mails. I'm sure you can get all the help you want if you ask for it.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: You're not allowed to join a cult.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: You can get a room at the international students' lodge. If you think you're going on a budget, check out the Utokyo lodge in Mitaka. It is one eighth as cheap as the others, but it is further away (public transport closes at around 00:30 and opens again around 05:00).

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: I had a common kitchen but all the lodges have different setups.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Check out the website. Komaba lodge is nice and so is the location.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The registration for faculty of law courses starts earlier and it't not just for law students. Check out the courses before you dismiss it. You could miss some great courses.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: A LOT of forms.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer:
You can probably ask for help with anything. The manuals are pretty helpful. 
If there is an issue with anything they will tell you... Or at least they told me.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer:
There is a great system of course registration and correction periods. 
As mentioned above, check out the courses for law before the deadline, if you're an undergraduate student.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: sign up for everything that sounds interesting and dump the ones you don't like in the course correction period. Also, Suginohara Masako is great. She teaches a nice course on international political economy, which is pretty basic at first but the articles and textbooks are great and it becomes better and better.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It's not crazy high. A lot of my peers didn't study very much, so if you do you can raise the level pretty easily. I took 7 courses that avaraged around 50 pages per week per class, ranging from 0-200.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More discussions, less group work. Some classes have participation grades.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
In order of how engaged I was:
1 Refugee and Forced Migration Studies
2 International Political Economy
3 Global Issues in a Divided and Vulnerable World
4 Regional Security Organizations
5 3rd Culture Children's Literature
6 Sustainability and Development in Asia
7 Start-ups and venture capital

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Two first courses mentioned above were really great. Looked forward to them every week.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
If you want to cook you have to buy pots and pans and everything. 
Also, I spent dkk 10.000 more than i thought i would in the first month. 
It was hard to adjust to JPY.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Oats and vegetables are really expensive. Eggs and juice are not.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
Sign-up was awkward. It's directed toward local students. 
tried to sign up for tennis but they never replied. 
Heard everything is easy if you speak Japanese.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go running. It's a great way to get to now the surrounding area by foot.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Take a hike.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: took two weeks.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Nope, sorry. Maybe sign up for buddy programme.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Shyness and language barriers

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The constant bowing and politeness. Most of the everyday encounters are just correographies

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Should've gotten the co-op card.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't sleep on the food trucks, Sleep in the library.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Got to get out the house and get some fresh academic air.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Long-distance relationship maybe... Idk... It was a nice trip.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Have fun, follow your heart

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
